name: counters_exist_even_at_zero
why: ENTRY Z-E1. Ten drawing entries are waiting to write surface finish, datum references, weld symbols and GD&T. **Four of the APIs that insert them return `Void`** — a button, not an API: they have no way to say they did nothing, and indeed they do not say so. Without an INDEPENDENT counter read from the state, each of those ten entries would be green on the word of the operation itself. This case puts the counters BEFORE the need.
defect_caught: A field that appears only when it has an interesting value teaches nobody to look for it: whoever does not find `surface_finish` concludes that the API cannot answer, not that the number is zero. Here the six numbers are demanded **all six, even all at zero** — and the bench treats a missing field as a RED proof (entry F4), so the expectation is true.
_and_the_sheet_is_counted_separately: Measured on 18/9/2026 and it changed the design of the field: the notes of the title block are on the SHEET, not on a view, and they are **sixty-seven** on this drawing template. `InsertNote` — today the only annotation API that works out of process — puts the note **on the sheet**: 67 -> 68, with all three views stuck at zero. Counting only the views, `note` would be a field that **cannot become true**, that is a promise and not a measurement. That is why the sheet has its own six numbers in a drawer of its own.

expect.why: the part the drawing is made on
a view attaches to the path of the part
the bench follows the new document (entry GT0)

steps._and_the_part_is_named_explicitly: See `title_block_says_what_it_wants`: without this line the drawing was made of the first part open, and nobody gave an error. The trouble started from this case — it is its part that ended up in the drawing of the other.

expect.why: real views are needed: the counters live on `IView`, and without views there would be nothing to ask them on

**THE PART THAT MAKES THE ENTRY WORTH IT, and it is the zero.** The field must be there even when there is nothing to count: the bench treats a missing field as a red proof (F4), so this expectation tells «zero» from «I do not know»
ditto: `InsertDatumTag()` returns `Void` and will never say whether it inserted. This number is the only way to know, and it must exist before the entry that uses it
read with `GetSFSymbolCount`, **not** `GetSurfaceFinishSymbolCount` — the name for symmetry with `InsertSurfaceFinishSymbol`, which does not exist

**THE VIEWS ARE EMPTY, AND HERE WE SEE WHETHER SOMEONE SUMMED THE SHEET.** If this number were sixty-seven instead of zero, it would mean that the notes of the title block ended up in the count of the views — and a drawing without a single annotation would look full

THE COUNTERPART, and without it the zero above would prove nothing: it would only prove that the counters always return zero. Sixty-seven is the title block of THIS workshop (`Disegno.drwdot`): if the drawing template changes, this expectation turns red **and it must** — the number of notes of the title block is not a detail of form, it is what the title block asks for
the field is there per view too, not only in the total. It is called «all» and not «total» because `GetAnnotationCount` **is not the sum** of the other five: it also counts the dimensions

the blindness travels with the answer: an annotation on a non-printing layer exists, is counted, and is not in the PDF. Whoever reads these numbers is reading the document, not what comes out of the printer
